note: Seen 2026-11-09. poweroff in pmOS boots pmOS again. title: The ADSP crashes every 13-25 s, restarting audio each time
note: Cause found 2026-11-09 by tracing every request the ADSP makes (a verbose hexagonrpcd build on the phone): the sensors service (hexagonrpcd -s) attaches the ADSP sensor process, whose registry init re-reads the sensor configs and needs to write (temp.json); hexagonrpcd refuses all writes, the firmware asserts (SNS_REG_INIT) and the whole ADSP restarts, taking audio with it. No registry state fixes it (packaged, or the phone own from persist, readable, with the version marker - which hexagonrpcd also never serves: a real gap, patch drafted). Fix in place on the phone: hexagonrpcd-adsp-sensorspd masked. Result: 0 ADSP crashes across three boots and many minutes, the POCO X3 sound card up at about 12 s, playback without crashes. Trade-off: no ADSP sensors, which did not work anyway. Next: propose upstream (do not start sensorspd on surya until registry writes are supported; serve sns_reg_version in hexagonrpcd); see sensors-registry-writes. Settled 2026-11-11: fixed by masking the audio processor's helper services (hexagonrpcd rootpd, sensorspd).

title: WCD937x device tree: drop aoncc, clock the VA macro from q6afecc
note: The boot hang (RCU stalls) with the WCD937x patch is the aoncc clock controller at 0x03380000, an SM8250 address with nothing near it in the SM7150 tree: with only aoncc disabled the phone boots (2026-11-09). Without aoncc the VA macro has no mclk, so the macros, SoundWire and the sound card stay deferred. Fix as SM8250 does: no aoncc, VA macro mclk from q6afecc. Audit tools and results in linux-phone-oco/surya-lab and on linux-phone-oco/linux#1. Settled 2026-11-11: in linux-phone-oco/linux pull request #1; the codec comes up.

title: ADSP sensors: let hexagonrpcd serve a writable sensor registry
note: The sensors firmware on SM7150 (surya) rebuilds its registry from the configs at start and writes temp.json beside it; hexagonrpcd refuses every write by design, and does not serve registry/../sns_reg_version either. Sensors need both: the version marker served (patch drafted against hexagonrpc v0.5.0-20) and writes to a per-device writable copy of the registry (as Android persist is writable). An upstream change to linux-msm/hexagonrpc; until then the sensors service stays off on surya.

title: One cold boot came up without audio services
note:
With the sensors service off, one boot (2026-11-09) never announced the ADSP audio services, so no sound card until the ADSP was restarted by hand. Not reproduced in two further valid cold boots (audio services about 0.1-0.2 s after the ADSP, card present). Watch for it; if it recurs, check whether the in-kernel pd-mapper was loaded before the ADSP booted.

2026-11-17: no longer rare - 3 of 8 boots that night (stock and test kernels alike) came up with the ADSP running but no audio services, so no sound card; restarting remoteproc0 (stop, start) brought the card back each time. The speaker's support is only as good as this; a fix, or at least a recovery at boot, is next after the microphone - or before it if it keeps recurring.

2026-11-17, read from the phone's journal (bring-up): in a bad boot the ADSP comes up but the APR audio services (aprsvc:service:4:3/4/7/8) are never added; in a good boot they appear 0.2 s after 'remote processor adsp is now up'. In the bad boot they appeared only right after the manual ADSP restart. So the protection-domain up notification (PDR, through the in-kernel PD mapper) never arrived. qcom_pd_mapper is a module nothing depends on (lsmod: used by 0), so it can load after the ADSP has booted. Next: load qcom_pd_mapper before the remoteprocs (modules-load.d through the device manifest, or the initramfs), count bad boots over twenty reboots before and after; then the kernel fix (pas depending on the PD mapper) for upstream.

2026-11-17 trial (bring-up): with /etc/modprobe.d/devlab-pd-mapper.conf on the phone (softdep qcom_q6v5_pas pre: qcom_pd_mapper) 13 of 13 boots came up with the sound card, against 8 failing of 42 health runs before. Other distributions do the same (omarchy puts qcom_pd_mapper in the initramfs for Snapdragon laptops). Next: twenty more boots, then carry the file in device.toml's flash overlays with its reason, and the kernel-side fix (the remoteproc driver depending on the PD mapper) for upstream.

Done 2026-11-17 (bring-up): 21 of 21 boots with the sound card since the PD mapper loads before the remoteproc driver; surya's device.toml now carries lab/devlab-pd-mapper.conf to /etc/modprobe.d in every flash. The kernel-side form for upstream is backlog upstream-pd-mapper-order.

title: Microphone: check, and make it work
note:
Taken up 2026-11-17 by the bring-up session, as the weakest link the data shows: audio-mic and audio-earpiece are both broken and two milestones rest on them (surya-sound, and the calls of surya-phone and lp-calls-and-messages), while the other broken parts (cameras, fingerprint, sensors) rest only on every-part and the modem waits for a SIM card. Where it stands (surya-audio/wcd-boots, 2026-11-11): with the LPI pin-mux fix (pins 19 and 23: swr_tx_data and swr_rx_data at their right function index) the WCD9375 enumerates on both SoundWire buses, binds, and the card POCO X3 is made with the codec's controls. Capture then fails at prepare: the TX SoundWire master (62ed0000) reads nothing back from the codec (swrm_wait_for_rd_fifo_avail read underflow, reading DPN_PortCtrl of port 1, addr 0x102), so Program transport params fails with -5 - also with the bus and codec held awake. Next: a health check that records from the main microphone and fails until it hears a signal (test first), then the read-back on the TX bus: compare the TX data pins and the controller's read settings with the vendor kernel and sibling SoCs (sm6150, sm7125).

2026-11-17, night (bring-up): the check mic-records runs after every boot (a known gap until it passes). In one-off test kernels the cause narrowed: about a millisecond after the sound card registers, the WCD9375 drops off both SoundWire buses at once and is never enumerated again, so the capture's port setup gets no answer. Ruled out: the clock-stop resume path, runtime suspend, headset detection, and any traced register write, supply or GPIO in that window. Lead: our device tree's active reset pin state drives the active-low reset low, where the vendor's drives it high. Next: a try with the reset's active state output-high, logging the bus-level SoundWire writes at card registration. Full record: surya-lab research/microphone.md.

2026-11-17, later (bring-up): the drop is explained and fixed - ASoC puts idle components into their sleep pin state, and the codec's sleep state held its reset low (traced to snd_soc_bind_card). Fixed on linux-phone-oco/linux PR #4 (with the SoundWire pin-mux fix as PR #3), both queued in upstream-queue for sm7150-mainline, waiting for the author to send. With it the codec stays attached and capture prepares, but delivers exact zeros. The built-in microphones are digital mics (TX DMIC1-3); this DSP rejects the VA capture port, so they go through the TX macro. Next: why the TX decimators deliver zeros (register sequence against the vendor's tx-macro), then the DMIC route. Tests use no sound louder than the author allows (lab-tools test-sound-level-setting).

2026-11-17, ~04:40 UTC (bring-up): THE MICROPHONE WORKS, on a test kernel built from branches (linux-phone-oco/linux test/surya-mic). The last fault: the capture link used the TX SoundWire controller's playback DAI (swr2 0); capture through DAI 1 (PR #6, found in pulpoff/linux-surya, a mainline surya tree on Mobian whose device tree also confirmed tonight's other fixes). surya's microphones are analog (ADC1 bottom, ADC2 top). Proof decided by the phone: surya's check mic-hears-speaker plays a 1 kHz tone at -6 dBFS and 20% volume (the author heard it: 'nice and soft') and finds it 57 dB above the noise - pass. All four fixes queued in upstream-queue for sm7150-mainline, waiting for the author. Next: the proven kernel as the phone's default (lab-tools kernel-promote, asked of the conveyor) so audio-mic leaves the known gaps and the face keeps works; then the top mic (ADC2), the headset mic, a UCM capture profile, and the earpiece through the WCD EAR PA.

Correction (2026-11-17, bring-up): where this item and research/microphone.md (steps 10, 11, 14) speak of surya's built-in microphones as digital mics, that reading came from the vendor's QRD reference board and is wrong for surya: its microphones are analog, WCD9375 ADC1 (bottom) and ADC2 via INP3 (top), both proven by mic-hears-speaker. The DMIC path is dropped (research decision 2026-11-17-microphones-analog-wcd-path). The kept kernel records with both on every boot; audio-mic left surya's known gaps. Queue from the research, in order: mic-ucm-capture, mic-held, mic-upstream, mic-dmic-dropped.

title: Plasma Mobile: speakers silent, the chain playing
note: Plasma Mobile (fresh Nura image, sound fixes applied on the phone): speakers were silent with the whole chain playing. Two causes, both confirmed: (1) the image restores a saved mixer state with both amplifiers' digital volume at 0 = -110 dB; (2) a tas2562 driver bug: setting the Digital Volume Control changes only the driver's cache, the chips (page 2, 0x0c-0x0f) stay at -110 dB. Writing 0x40000000 straight into both chips with i2cset made sound work: the user heard YouTube in Firefox, 2026-11-10. Not persistent: after a power-off the restore and the driver bug bring the silence back. Needed: the driver fix (upstream-tas2562-volume), and until then a boot-time step that writes the volume into the chips. Root cause found and fixed 2026-11-10: the tas2562 driver's maximum volume (0 dB) read past the end of its lookup table, which muted the amps; with two more faults (the latch byte written first, resume skipping bytes). Fixed module installed and proven on the phone by I2C reads; every flash bakes it in. Listen on Plasma when it is next run.

title: The audio DSP crashes right after resume from suspend
note: Trigger found 2026-11-10, one change at a time: with hexagonrpcd's RootPD helper (a FastRPC client) attached, the audio DSP dies on every suspend attempt - 24 of 24 (fatal error EX:kernel:0x0:IST46:0x132:PC=0xf0049be4, about 30 ms after the attempt; the attempts abort at once because the USB link cannot go idle). Without the helper: 0 of 8, and on a clean boot with it masked 0 of 9, all checks passing; sound does not need it. Not a first-boot effect, not the sensor proxy, no stream open. The earlier "rare" crash (2 of 28, both early in a boot) was the same one: there the helper died with the first crashes and stayed down. Fixed in the lab: hexagonrpcd-adsp-rootpd masked in the device manifest, baked in at every flash. Still open, for upstream: why an attached FastRPC client makes the DSP assert across a suspend attempt (the kernel's fastrpc and remoteproc suspend handling, or hexagonrpcd), and why the helper restarts after each crash on a fresh system. Settled 2026-11-11: fixed with the same masks and the awake service.

title: A device template: the conveyor any phone's support is built on
note:
Asked for 2026-11-10: the conveyor as a repo of its own, so anyone can bring support to another phone with the same conveyors, CI, tests, tad page and automatic integration into the grand picture; surya is the first instance, not the mould.

Design. (1) linux-phone-oco/device-template, a GitHub template repository: Use this template makes <vendor>-<codename>-lab. (2) device.toml, one manifest per device - codename, SoC, compatible strings, panel variants, image sources, how to reach the phone - read by every script; no script edited per device. (3) Generic machinery, generalized from surya-lab: the phone library (USB or Wi-Fi, commands on stdin), flashing with built-in fixes, provisioning (packages, Wi-Fi from private files), switching shells, device-tree audits, an upstream queue with send commands generated by get_maintainer.pl. (4) Tests as small independent checks, one file each declaring its component and what it needs, so a device runs the checks that apply; results as JSON lines with a versioned schema. (5) Device-independent analysis in linux-phone-oco/lab-tools (Rust): tone (speaker tests microphone) first. (6) Onboarding conveyor: a lab-tools command reads a running phone (compatible, inputs, outputs, sound devices) and fills device.toml - and from the same facts generates the Sxmo device profile. (7) Each device repo publishes its own tad data (support status, test runs, wiki claims) with CI that validates it and renders its page. (8) Integration: a feed in linux-phone-oco/docs discovers device repos by a GitHub topic and pulls their published tables, so a new device appears in the devices table and the support grid (tad draws device x component as a matrix) with no hand edits. (9) Conventions in AGENTS.md: explicit intent for state changes, lists as arguments, secrets outside repos, fingerprints before trusting images. (10) Proof: surya-lab re-based onto the template as its first instance - still 18 of 18 through it. Landscape read 2026-11-10 (see the landscape table): build on what exists - device.toml derives from postmarketOS deviceinfo; tests take the shape of pmOS's initramfs CI tests and use bootrr for driver probes; the lab aims to be a CI-tron-compatible setup and surya a device under test in pmOS's hardware farm; flashing leans on pmbootstrap. 

2026-11-17: made - linux-phone-oco/device-template (a GitHub template): a lab is device.toml, tests/health, tests/results and its records; every tool is devlab's. Proven on surya the same day: the phone checks its own health after every boot (devlab-health, a static Rust runner, generic checks in postmarketOS's test shape, [health] in the manifest, known gaps measured but not ill health), every change devlab makes ends with that report, devlab gather now files the runs here (9 runs filed, a week of filing by hand caught up), devlab mcp is the door for agents. Open: surya-lab re-based onto it, a second phone through it, device.toml read off a running phone, the Alpine package through the package conveyor.

title: The device toolset in Rust, for any phone

Asked for 2026-11-10: tooling must not be tied to surya - surya is the test subject; the work is a conveyor for any phone, built as one Rust toolset (rust-script for small scripts) as we go, informed by existing projects (postmarketOS tooling first). Plan: one CLI in linux-phone-oco/lab-tools reading the device manifest (device.toml): phone (find over USB or Wi-Fi, run commands with no quoting layer), kernel install/try/log/remove (the safe test-kernel boot proven on surya 2026-11-10: one try by boot counting, a stalled initramfs saves its log and reboots into stock), provision, test (the checks, results as versioned JSON lines), tone. Port surya-lab's shell tools one at a time behind tests; surya-lab shrinks to data and a manifest - the first step of device-template. Read first, as reference and to reuse conventions: pmbootstrap (flasher, initfs, sideload, ci), postmarketos-mkinitfs hooks, pmaports CI and testing.

title: The phone kept reconnecting on the host's USB

title: Deep sleep measured once: the SoC's own counters across one suspend
note: The first step of decision 2026-11-17-deep-sleep-measured-s2idle; it settles the biggest unknown - does surya's SoC reach its floor at all on mainline? On USB the phone cannot suspend (the link cannot go idle, and devlab-usb-awake holds a wake lock), so the lab has never measured a sleep. One sleep, falling back by itself: the USB gadget let go (soft_connect), the lab's and Sxmo's wake locks released, s2idle for 60 s woken by the RTC (rtcwake -m freeze), the gadget reconnected; qcom_stats (cxsd, aosd, ddr, adsp, cdsp, modem), suspend_stats, the cluster domain's idle states and every wakeup source's count read before and after. Wanted from the conveyor: this as a devlab verb (lab-tools backlog health-suspend-cycle, where what this needs of it is written), so it is never typed by hand. Proven by: the check soc-sleeps, run in the same boot after the sleep (devlab suite run), says pass or fail instead of skip - a number either way. Expected: fail, with the reasons in its detail.

title: surya's own cluster sleep parameters in its device tree
note: sm7150.dtsi asks the firmware for SC7180's cluster states 0x41001244 and 0x4100b244 with surya's latencies; surya's own Android tables have cx-off 0x224 and llcc-off 0xc24, that is 0x41002244 and 0x4100c244 (SM8150 uses 0x4100c244 too); the deepest state was never entered once at runtime (research sm7150-cluster-params). A dt/ branch in linux-phone-oco/linux changing the two parameters, tried with devlab kernel try, then the measured sleep of sleep-measured-once on it. Proven by: soc-sleeps passes (cxsd above 0) where it failed on today's parameters, and the cluster domain's deepest state is entered; the health suite otherwise unchanged. Then upstream: a patch for the SM7150 series (sm7150-mainline; the upstreaming series is to be resent) through upstream-queue.

title: The audio DSP sleeps when nothing plays
note: Read 2026-11-17: the audio DSP never slept once in a boot (qcom_stats adsp 0, against about 200 for the compute DSP and the modem), with no stream open but the VA, TX and RX macros active and soundwire_qcom.stay_awake=1 on the test kernel's command line (from the microphone hunt). A DSP that never sleeps holds CX up, and with it the SoC. First try without stay_awake, then find which LPASS vote stays up with no stream (the macros' clocks through q6prm, as a QCS8550 port found its LPASS votes held the floor). Proven by: soc-sleeps no longer lists adsp among the processors never asleep, and passes; the sound checks still pass.

title: FastRPC helpers stopped across suspend; the sensors back
note: With hexagonrpcd's rootpd helper attached the audio DSP crashed on every suspend attempt (24 of 24), so it and the sensors helper are masked and the sensors are gone (surya-lab: sensors-without-crash). postmarketOS stops the helper before suspend and starts it after on the Pixel 3a for the same crash. Do the same on surya with a systemd sleep hook, then unmask both helpers. Proven by: in one boot after a measured sleep, motion-and-light passes, soc-sleeps passes and no audio DSP crash is counted on resume. Upstream question kept: why an attached FastRPC client makes the DSP assert across suspend.

title: Waking from deep sleep for calls and messages
note: On the floor reached above: the modem's IPCRTR glink wakeup enabled (/sys/bus/rpmsg/devices/4080000.remoteproc:glink-edge.IPCRTR.-1.-1/power/wakeup), ModemManager's quick suspend/resume quieting the modem before suspend, and Sxmo's post-wake hook putting the phone back to sleep when the wake was not a call or a message (as postmarketOS does on the OnePlus 6; still reported unreliable there, pmaports 4989). Needs a SIM card - the author's hands. Proven by: a witnessed test wakes-for-call, to be entered in tests (a call to the sleeping phone rings within 5 s; an SMS sent to it arrives), and soc-sleeps passing in the same boot.

title: Sound recorded through the microphone
note:
Two tries on 2026-11-11 in the test kernel. The Android route sets cleanly (TX DEC0 MUX=SWR_MIC, TX SMIC MUX0=ADC0, TX_AIF1_CAP Mixer DEC0, ADC1_MIXER, ADC1, MultiMedia2 Mixer TX_CODEC_DMA_TX_3) and the card's routing wires mic bias to AMIC1-3. Starting the capture stream fails: the TX SoundWire bus can no longer read from the codec (read underflow at DPN_PortCtrl of port 1; 'Program transport params failed'), so no recording is made. Not power management: the same with the bus, macros and codec kept awake. Next lead: the moment of failure is when the bus is reshaped for the stream - compare the TX controller's frame and port parameters with the phone's Android kernel. Compared with the Android kernel: the TX bus's port layout and timings match (ports 2-5 as on sm8250 mainline and the vendor), so not the port table. The first read of a port register (DP1 PortCtrl) at stream prepare fails while hundreds of codec register accesses worked at init. Next: trace the bus's transfers (dynamic debug on the SoundWire bus and the qcom controller, or a kernel with SoundWire debugfs - this one has none). Parked 2026-11-12: the lab-agent redesign after the 2026-11-11 incident comes first; resume from the next step above (order: open-commons-observatory decision 2026-11-12-the-redesign-first).

Done 2026-11-17 (bring-up): sound is recorded through both microphones on the kept kernel and through the UCM profile; proven by mic-hears-speaker and mic-top-hears-speaker. See docs backlog microphone and mic-ucm-capture.

title: The microphone codec times out at initialisation
note: Solved 2026-11-11: the audio pin driver muxed gpio19 (TX SoundWire data) to function 1 and gpio23 (RX data) to 3, where the phone's own Android kernel has 3 and 2. With both corrected the TX bus no longer clashes, the codec initialises and the sound card is made with the codec on it. The clocks going to 0 were a consequence, not the cause.

title: The modem stays in shutting-down and will not go online

The loop: the modem writes /readwrite/lctoem.tmp, reads it back with rsize=0 seek=0, and itself ends the transfer at once - the option handling the Fairphone fix (pmaports !4747) changed. Next: compare tqftpserv 1.1.1 with upstream's rsize and seek handling, look at what the modem wrote, then one try with a fixed build. No calls, messages or data without the author's word.

title: Call audio both ways: q6voice, with the uplink from the microphone
note: What pulpoff/linux-surya found on this phone (research-microphones, 2026-11-17): on a modem call the ADSP mixes the audio itself (MVM, CVS, CVP over APR); the host starts the AFE ports and the voice processor. q6voice from sdm845-mainline with the CVD 2.3 set-up SM7150 needs, a hostless VoiceMMode1 link (q6voiced opens it per call), routing 'TERT_MI2S_RX Voice Mixer VoiceMMode1' and 'VoiceMMode1 Capture Mixer TX_CODEC_DMA_TX_3'. The far end hears nothing unless a 1-channel capture actually runs on TX_CODEC_DMA_TX_3 during the call; the default TX topology 0x10F71 sends silence without Xiaomi's calibration, 0x10F70 (none) works; the top mic picks up less speaker echo. Proven by a test that runs the removal under sh in a fake boot tree (lab-tools kernel.rs); on surya, mic and ear were installed before entries said their release, so removing ear removes its own files only.

title: A device-tree change is one boot: kernel try --dtb
note: Asked by bring-up, 2026-11-17: a device-tree experiment on the kept kernel took unkeep, a stock reboot, try and keep again. devlab kernel try NAME --dtb FILE now boots installed kernel NAME's kernel, initramfs and modules once with the new device tree (entry NAME-dt, one try, sorted ahead of the kept kernel, never blessed, its release said so remove keeps the modules), and a try is judged by the entry the bootloader says it booted (LoaderEntrySelected, read on surya) rather than by the release's name, which two entries can share. Proven by tests and by running the entry script in a fake boot tree; not yet tried live (the phone's experiments are bring-up's).

title: Upstream: the ADSP must not boot before the in-kernel PD mapper
note: Found 2026-11-17 on surya (bring-up): remoteproc's qcom_common only adds an auxiliary pd-mapper device when it prepares a remote processor; qcom_pd_mapper is a module that udev loads later, so on about one boot in five the ADSP asks for its domains before the mapper answers and its audio PD never comes up (no APR services, no sound card). Worked around in the device lab with 'softdep qcom_q6v5_pas pre: qcom_pd_mapper' (21 of 21 boots good); other distributions put qcom_pd_mapper in the initramfs (omarchy, Snapdragon laptops). Next: check lore for an existing fix; otherwise a patch (a MODULE_SOFTDEP in qcom_q6v5_pas or qcom_common, or making the mapper built-in where remoteproc is), queued for the author; and for postmarketOS, qcom_pd_mapper in the SM7150 initramfs modules.
